charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Wholesale Funding Mix: Borrowings vs Debt Securities in Issue
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

bankInterestIncome.title: Gross interest income
bankInterestIncome.content:
Gross interest income is interest earned on the loan book, securities and interbank placements, before deducting the interest SMFG pays on deposits and wholesale funding -- that net figure is net interest income, not shown here.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the roughly 3x jump from FY2022 (¥1.75tn) to FY2026 (¥6.93tn) tracks the end of Bank of Japan negative-rate policy and the global rate-hiking cycle, not loan growth -- yen rates moved far more than the loan book did.

What to watch:

  • Gross interest income rising faster than the loan book implies margin expansion, not just volume
  • A reversal if the BoJ cuts rates back down
  • Compare against funding cost growth (Borrowings, deposits) to see if the spread is widening or narrowing

fundingMix.title: Wholesale funding mix
fundingMix.content:
Borrowings are mostly short-term interbank and central-bank funding (including Bank of Japan facilities); debt securities in issue are bonds and commercial paper SMFG issues directly to investors. Both sit alongside customer deposits -- not shown in this CSV -- as the bank's three funding sources.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the mix has shifted since FY2022 -- Borrowings nearly halved (¥20.6tn → ¥10.6tn) while debt securities in issue grew (¥11.4tn → ¥16.6tn), a move from short-dated interbank funding toward longer-dated, more stable market funding as rates normalised.

What to watch:

  • A rising share of debt securities generally means more stable, less rollover-sensitive funding
  • A spike in Borrowings can signal reliance on central-bank liquidity facilities
  • Funding cost direction here feeds straight into the net interest margin the bank earns

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
